newsitem.title: USA: Car thief charged with causing distant accident.
newsitem.headline: Car thief charged with causing distant accident.

text.p: A car thief has been indicted for involuntary manslaughter for a fatal accident in which he was not directly involved.
Paul Lovelace, 25, was indicted by a county grand jury even though he was nowhere near the June 15 accident scene in downtown Cincinnati, Hamilton County Prosecutor Joseph Deters said.
An 18-year-old man was killed and two female companions seriously injured when a police cruiser -- responding to an area-wide high-speed pursuit of Lovelace -- ran a red light and struck their car.

Deters said the accident would never have happened if it had not been for a 35-mile chase through Northern Kentucky and Cincinnati precipitated by Lovelace's refusal to stop his vehicle and surrender.
Involuntary manslaughter carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison.

Police Officer Gregory Berting, 23, a rookie still on probation, was fired from the force Tuesday for causing the accident by failing to follow police guidelines in chase situations. He was attempting to link up with the pursuit when the crash happened.
Deters said local authorities were still reviewing Berting's case to determine if vehicular homicide charges should be filed against him.
